raw_case_text: A 50-year-old Caucasian male, with no relevant past medical records, was referred to SCT with a high-risk acute lymphoblastic B leukemia in first complete remission (CR). Allogeneic SCT was performed with peripheral blood stem cells from an unrelated Portuguese matched 9/10 donor (disparity in locus HLA-A), after myeloablative conditioning regimen (with busulfan, cyclophosphamide, and antilymphocytic serum). Graft versus host disease prophylaxis was performed with tacrolimus and methotrexate. There were no major complications during neutropenic period. Corticotherapy was prescribed for upper digestive graft versus host disease diagnosed 2 months after SCT. In the following months, patient developed mild fluctuating cytopenias, mostly thrombocytopenia (between 60 and 80*109/L). The only significant complaint was intermittent tiredness. Bone marrow evaluation had no signs of relapse disease and patient had complete chimerism. The common causes for thrombocytopenia were excluded:no evidence of graft versus host disease; no signs of viral or bacterial infection; and no signs of relapsed disease/dysplastic changes. The bone marrow smear performed 12 months after transplant revealed an unsuspected diagnosis: a massive bone marrow infiltration with amastigotes:(Figure 1 optical microscopy, Wright Giemsa stain, 100x magnification). Reticuloendothelial cells had exuberant parasitic cytoplasmatic inclusions and a few images of erythrophagocytosis were present (Figure 1). The sample was sent to DNA PCR analysis and Leishmania infantum was identified. Previous bone marrow smears were reviewed and scarce parasites, not previously observed, were found in a smear performed 6 months after SCT. The donor had no history of visceral leishmaniasis. The patient was treated with a total dose of 24 mg/kg of liposomal amphotericin B, with clinical improvement and no signs of leishmania in the bone marrow. Five months later, the patient developed epigastric pain and duodenal biopsy revealed no evidence of graft versus host disease but the presence of inflammatory infiltrate with the presence of amastigotes in the macrophages was evident; a new bone marrow was performed and was positive for leishmania. The patient restarted liposomal amphotericin B and a prolonged maintenance treatment is planned.

subjective.chief_complaint: A 50-year-old male presented with intermittent tiredness and fluctuating cytopenias 12 months after allogeneic stem cell transplantation.
subjective.history_of_present_illness: A 50-year-old male with acute lymphoblastic B leukemia in first complete remission underwent allogeneic peripheral blood stem cell transplantation (SCT). Conditioning included busulfan, cyclophosphamide, and antilymphocytic serum, with tacrolimus and methotrexate for GVHD prophylaxis. Upper digestive GVHD occurred at 2 months post-SCT and was treated with corticosteroids. Over subsequent months, he developed mild fluctuating cytopenias, predominantly thrombocytopenia (platelets 60-80 x 10^9/L), and intermittent tiredness. Bone marrow evaluation at 6 months showed complete chimerism without leukemia relapse. Bone marrow biopsy at 12 months post-SCT revealed parasitic infiltration, and antileishmanial therapy was initiated. Five months later, he developed new-onset epigastric pain, prompting upper endoscopy and repeat bone marrow evaluation.
subjective.past_medical_history: High-risk acute lymphoblastic B leukemia in first complete remission; allogeneic stem cell transplantation from an unrelated Portuguese 9/10 matched donor (HLA-A disparity). Upper gastrointestinal GVHD diagnosed 2 months post-SCT. Donor had no history of visceral leishmaniasis. No other relevant past medical records.
subjective.review_of_systems: Intermittent tiredness, mild fatigue; later developed epigastric pain. Denied fever, chills, night sweats, nausea, vomiting, or diarrhea.

objective.physical_examination: No peripheral lymphadenopathy or hepatosplenomegaly on initial examination. Epigastric tenderness noted at 5-month follow-up. Vital signs remained stable.
objective.routine_investigations: Mild fluctuating cytopenias, primarily thrombocytopenia (platelet count between 60 and 80 x 10^9/L). Bone marrow chimerism analysis demonstrated 100% complete donor chimerism. Viral and bacterial serological and molecular testing negative. No morphologic or flow cytometric signs of leukemia relapse or myelodysplastic changes.
objective.advanced_workup: Bone marrow aspiration and smear at 12 months post-transplant showed massive infiltration of reticuloendothelial cells with abundant parasitic cytoplasmic inclusions and erythrophagocytosis (retrospective review identified scarce inclusions at 6 months post-SCT). Duodenal biopsy at 17 months showed chronic inflammatory infiltrate with intracellular inclusions in macrophages, with no histological evidence of GVHD.

assessment_and_plan.assessment_and_confirmation:
Definitive Diagnosis: Allogeneic stem cell transplant-associated visceral leishmaniasis with secondary duodenal mucosal involvement.
Diagnostic Confirmation: Bone marrow aspirate smear revealed massive infiltration by Leishmania amastigotes; DNA PCR identified Leishmania infantum. Repeat bone marrow aspirate and duodenal biopsy at 5 months demonstrated recurrent Leishmania amastigotes within macrophages.
Differentials Ruled Out: Leukemic relapse, myelodysplastic syndrome, graft-versus-host disease (GVHD) recurrence, bacterial or opportunistic viral infections (CMV, EBV).
Treatment & Clinical Course: Initially treated with intravenous liposomal amphotericin B at a cumulative dose of 24 mg/kg, resulting in clinical improvement and parasite clearance from bone marrow. Following relapse with epigastric pain and duodenal involvement at 5 months, liposomal amphotericin B was reinitiated with a planned prolonged maintenance regimen.
